node-1.label: A 2-month-old male infant presented with a progressively enlarging purplish-red mass in the right lower limb since birth.

node-2.label: The mass measured approximately 5 × 5 cm with purplish-red discoloration and surrounding tissue swelling; physical examination revealed a 5 × 5 cm mass at the right knee joint that was warm to touch, of medium consistency, and well-defined; hemorrhagic spots were noted on the upper hard palate.

node-3.label: Past medical history, personal history, and immunization status were normal; there were no postnatal episodes of cyanosis, convulsions, or bleeding; family history was negative for congenital malformations, tumors, or hemorrhagic conditions.

node-4.label: Vital signs were stable, the infant was alert, and no abnormalities were detected in the central nervous, cardiovascular, or respiratory systems.

attrs.why: The Laboratory_Physician expert analysis states that benign tumor, malformation, and malignancy are refuted. The severe thrombocytopenia, hypofibrinogenemia, prolonged coagulation times, elevated D-dimer, and anemia are atypical for a simple benign vascular tumor, so confidence remains low at 0.15.

The Laboratory_Physician expert analysis does not support vascular malformation; the severe consumptive coagulopathy and enhancing vascular mass are better explained by Kasabach-Merritt syndrome. Confidence remains 0.05.

The Laboratory_Physician expert analysis explicitly states that severe thrombocytopenia, hypofibrinogenemia, prolonged PT/APTT/TT, high D-dimer, anemia, palate hemorrhagic spots, and the enhancing inguinal/thigh vascular mass strongly support Kasabach-Merritt syndrome. These findings match the existing laboratory and imaging evidence, so confidence remains 0.85.

The Laboratory_Physician expert analysis refutes malignancy; the stable infant without constitutional symptoms and the coagulopathy profile are more consistent with Kasabach-Merritt syndrome. Confidence remains 0.05.

node-10.label: PT/APTT/TT are prolonged and D-dimer is 21.29
